alternate_names: Sri Santhana Venu Gopala Swamy Temple, Kallur

history.summary: The Lord Venu Gopala Swami temple at Kallur, documented as the 'Sri Santhana Venu Gopala Swamy Temple, Kallur' on JustDial (4.7 stars, 52 ratings) — the major pilgrimage shrine of Kallur town. DATE CONFLICT: both TripGuyde (2019) and the Telangana government Bhadradri-Khammam districts profile call it '400 years old' yet also attribute its construction to the Kakatiya queen Rudrama Devi, who ruled in the 13th century — the two claims are incompatible, so the founding date is flagged as unverified. Distinct from the nearby ancient Shiva temple at Kallur attributed to the Kakatiya king Prataparudra, with five lingas and a large temple tank (per the same government profile); the two Kallur temples are separate shrines. IMAGE FLAG: no verified image of the Kallur temple exists after a genuine search (image results were all other towns' Venu Gopala temples), so media is empty. COORD FLAG: the geocoder returns only a different shrine (Venugopala Swamy Temple, Mudigonda, ~45 km away) for this name, so town-level Kallur coordinates are used — verify locally. CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV town 'Khammam' is wrong — the temple is at Kallur town, ~50 km from Khammam town; corrected to Kallur. District (Khammam) and state (Telangana) are correct.

name: Lord Venu Gopala Swami Temple (Kallur)
town_description: Kallur (Kalluru) is a town and mandal headquarters in Khammam district, Telangana, about 50 km from Khammam town. It was once a Qutub Shahi taluka headquarters and is known for its cluster of old temples, including the Venu Gopala Swami temple and nearby Shiva shrines.

travel.road: Kallur is ~50 km from Khammam town by road
